title: Clinical-biomechanical assessment of the rehabilitation of tibial fractures with pain-adapted weight bearing
summary: The release of a pain-adapted weight bearing during the early rehabilitation phase after surgically treated tibial shaft fracture is increasingly applied in postoperative treatment. Nevertheless, the clinical and biomechanical effectiveness of this post-treatment directive is still inadequately researched. Although there are indications of a positive clinical impact of an initial pain-adapted increase in weight bearing in some studies, a restrictive limitation of load (such as a 20 kg partial load) is still the common clinical practice in Germany. The aim of this study is to examine the biomechanical, clinical, and functional changes associated with a newly introduced pain-adapted load directive in the clinical setting for patients with tibial shaft fracture. Patients with unilateral tibial shaft fracture treated with an intramedullary nail will be reassessed according to their pain-adapted load directive over a 12-month follow-up. A comparison to assess the postoperative healing process will be made based on biomechanical and clinically collected parameters. To evaluate the effectiveness of clinical practice based on prescribed load directives, postoperative bone healing and implant stability, physical function, and gait biomechanics will be compared. The results of this study aim to contribute to assessing the safety of the new loading protocol, thereby better understanding the effect of load prescriptions on bone healing and gait biomechanics after tibial shaft fracture.

interventions.name:
Postoperative observational study (follow-up: 2, 3, 6 and 12 months)
Biomechanical movement and load analysis of the gait pattern
Degree of fracture healing (RUST score)
Subjective movement function (SMFA score)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Acute traumatic unilateral and complete tibial shaft fracture (AO classification 42-A to C) with or without an additional fibula fracture
Operative treatment with an intramedullary nail at the BG Hospital Murnau
Exclusion criteria:
further injuries of the lower extremity
neurological conditions affecting gait
BMI ≥ 31
patient is unable to comprehend the study project
